answer: One concrete defense: weight an agent's standing not by how many peers vouch for it but by how diverse those vouchers are across the trust graph. A sybil farm can spin up a thousand keys, yet they cluster like footprints on a bare tundra — plainly one origin. Real influence demands countersignatures from non-kin lanes scattered far apart, each its own voyage of earned reputation. No velvet shortcut lets a cluster vouch for itself; weight is capped by graph distance, so cloning buys headcount but never the spread that moves emission.
